reputation.summary: The benchmark ultralow-noise bipolar single. Builders use it for MC phono head amps (audioXpress MC100, Wyn Palmer MC preamp), mic preamps and DAC I/V stages, and it has long been set against the OPA627 in Head-Fi and diyAudio debates. Japanese reviewers reportedly call its sound 'satin-finish', robust and crisper than the OPA627 (not re-verified). Soomal (China) groups it with the AD847 as famous for big dynamics, a grand sound and powerful bass. Soomal's Creative AE-9 review says the AD797 (and OPA1611) had better dynamics and resolution than the NE5534 but sounded too hard to be pleasing there. Engineering sources use it as a reference low-noise part. Its place in Samuel Groner's distortion survey is unverified.
sonic_descriptors: satin-finish, high-quality sound (Zigsow JP; not re-verified)
robust, full-bodied; crisper and more 'digital' than OPA627 (JP reviews; not re-verified)
huge dynamics, grand sound, powerful bass (Soomal: 以动态大，声音大气，低频气势十足闻名)
ADI-style emphasised bass and treble with powerful but dry bass; Soomal says AD847/AD797 share the trend
better dynamics and resolution than NE5534 but too hard, not pleasing (Soomal AE-9 review: 偏硬，不够讨喜)
typical_uses: moving-coil phono head amps and RIAA preamps
microphone and mixing-console preamps
DAC I/V converters
test and measurement low-noise front ends (e.g. precision current sources, sonar LNAs)
single-channel op-amp rolling, usually on a dual adapter
caveats: Sensitive to layout, decoupling and capacitive load, so it is not a safe blind drop-in for rolling. The datasheet has a 'Driving Capacitive Loads' section (radiolocman Rev. K p.13).
Single only. Dual sockets need an adapter board, which adds lead length and oscillation risk.

High current noise (about 2 pA/√Hz) makes it a poor fit for high source or feedback impedances. One builder's datasheet review found it runs at gain 2, correcting an earlier 'needs gain ≥10' assumption, but loses its e_n advantage in a 20 kΩ network through i_n×R.
Draws about 8 mA per amplifier, more than typical audio duals.
Heavily counterfeited, especially DIP parts (including ANZ) and any metal-can 'AD797'.
Sonic descriptors are subjective and mostly single-source forum or review impressions.

families.counterfeit_notes: Counterfeiting is heavy. A 2021 diyAudio thread ('*Thousands Sold*, Great Reviews... Received Fake AD797 Like LM741. Did You Buy These?') reports thousands of fakes sold on eBay (over 2,500 in five-packs alone; seller AdeleParts2010). They behaved like LM741s: 33.8 nV/√Hz noise against the genuine 0.9 nV/√Hz, about 1 mA supply current against 8.2 mA, and 0.3 V to 0.9 V offset against 80 µV max. Pin 8 was open circuit, and the offset-null network looked like an LM741's. Negative eBay feedback later disappeared. A Head-Fi thread ('Cheapish AD797 and OPA627 on eBay, fakes?') and a Polish audiostereo.pl thread ('AD797ANZ fake or not') report the same problem; neither was re-checked. Soomal (China) says ADI never made a metal-can AD797, so every gold metal-can 'AD797' is fake (Soomal's statement, not an ADI document). Screening: (1) measure quiescent current, about 8 mA per part; (2) measure offset (≤80 µV) and noise; (3) check pin 8 for a diode junction; (4) reject metal cans and unusually cheap DIP AN/BN/ANZ. Buy only from authorized distributors.

families.name: LM833 / LM833-N (LM837 quad)
families.tagline: Cheap, quiet (4.5 nV/rtHz, 15-16 MHz, 7 V/us) bipolar audio dual found throughout consumer and pro gear; the budget sibling of the NE5532.
families.technology: Bipolar dual op-amp, internally compensated. Several different dies are sold under the one generic number. National's LM833 (TI LM833-N today) has a complementary emitter-follower output that uses a vertical PNP. TI's own LM833 (SLOS481, July 2010) has a quasi-complementary output made from two NPNs (TI E2E 430833). In E2E thread 1443925 a responder said TI's MC33078 and LM833 appear to be the same die because all specs and graphs are identical. Motorola/onsemi and ST have their own versions. TI confirmed on E2E (thread 1652528; reported by Hackaday 3 June 2026 and Headphonesty July 2026) that its NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 now share one die.

reputation.summary: A budget, low-noise (4.5 nV/rtHz) bipolar audio dual that datasheets aim at 'all preamp and high level stages in PCM and HiFi systems'. Common in CD players, portable players, graphic equalizers and DIY mic preamps, and usually weighed against the NE5532. GroupDIY forum posters (search-summary level) describe it as having lower distortion but lower output drive than the 5532, suited to high-gain/low-distortion work where drive is not needed, and as National's attempt to rival the 5532 that did not beat it. A search summary attributes to Mithat Konar's 2026 blog the view that the LM833 now out-specs the revised TI NE5532 in most respects. No verified sound descriptors or published measurements (Self, Groner, ASR) were found; treat as thin.

Hackaday (3 June 2026) and Headphonesty (July 2026) reported it, the latter describing the merged design as RC4580-based with NPN inputs and a complementary output stage. families.name: LM4562 / LME49720 / LME49710 / LME49740 (National ultra-low-distortion bipolar audio op-amps)
families.tagline: National's 2006-07 audio op-amp with 2.7 nV/rtHz noise and 0.00003% THD+N; the standard NE5532 'upgrade', with the metal-can HA versions as collector items.
families.technology: Bipolar input, voltage feedback, unity-gain stable; 55 MHz GBW, ±2.5 V to ±17 V supply. LM4562 (dual) and LME49720 (dual) are one die sold under two part numbers (per TI E2E). LME49710 is the single and LME49740 the quad of the same series. Inputs have differential protection diodes. Packages: SOIC (MA), PDIP (NA), TO-99 metal can (HA; dual and single only). Under TI PCN 20180308002 (March 2018), LM4562/LME49720 wafer production moved from a 150 mm line to TI's RFAB (Richardson, TX), on a newer process with a die-shrink redesign. Part numbers did not change.

lineage.notes: LM4562 released Aug 2006 (National document number 201572 per alldatasheet summaries). LME49710 followed in Nov 2006 and the LME49740 quad in Feb 2007. The LME49720 was a marketing rename in Mar 2007. National also offered the LME49860 (±22 V) in the same series. National-era parts with lot codes starting 'JR' came from the Greenock (UK) wafer fab, with assembly in Malaysia (per diyAudio).

TI reissued the datasheets in TI format in April 2013 (SNAS326J, SNAS393C, SNAS376C, SNAS377B), then SNAS326K (Dec 2013) and SNAS393D (Nov 2016). In 2015 TI announced a process-node end of life and suggested OPA1611/OPA1602 as replacements. Forum and E2E accounts say the 6-inch wafer line went away and the part was resurrected on an 8-inch line. PCN 20180308002 (March 2018) moved LM4562/LME49720 to RFAB, Richardson TX, with a die-shrink redesign. The E2E answer names the source fab as SFAB, Sherman TX; a diyAudio thread title says 'GB to US'. Forum posts say LM4562 prices dropped sharply in early 2019. TO-99 packages were on lifebuy from c.2017.

reputation.summary: Hi-Fi op-amp rollers and DIY builders treat this as the default 'better than NE5532' part. Its distortion measures near the limits of test equipment. NwAvGuy's 2011 op-amp measurements are often cited in its favour; the discovery sweep paraphrases him as saying it matches 'any elite part' (wording not re-checked). It is reported as a stock or socketed part in Asus Xonar and Creative Sound Blaster cards (exact part per card not re-checked), and it is widely used in Chinese DACs. Listeners call it neutral, clear, transparent and detailed, and sometimes 'clinical'. Japanese folklore holds that the LME49720 marking sounds brighter and the LM4562 bassier, although TI says the silicon is the same. Forum posters single out the TO-99 HA versions. All of these are subjective, unblinded reports.
sonic_descriptors: 'too clear' on violins (diyAudio, comparing it with LME49723)
LME49720: brighter, glossier; LM4562: bassier, denser (Japanese folklore, same die)
cleaner treble than a discrete stage (Soomal)
typical_uses: NE5532/4580 replacement in CD players, DACs and sound cards
DAC I/V and output stages
headphone amplifier gain stages
phono and mic preamps (LME49710HA prized)
pro-audio line stages (±17 V max)
low-noise RF/SDR audio and IQ stages (seen in GitHub SDR projects)
caveats: 55 MHz GBW: can oscillate in some sockets, adapters and layouts; needs good local decoupling

Since 2018 (PCN 20180308002), LM4562/LME49720 use a die-shrink die from RFAB under the same part number. Old-vs-new sound or measurement claims are unverified.

silicon_changes.when: PCN 20180308002 issued March 2018 (Mouser copy 20180309, revision -001 dated 20180326); new-die supply from c.2018-2019
silicon_changes.identification: The part number and marking are unchanged. Use the lot or date code. Per diyAudio, lots starting 'JR' were fabbed in Greenock (UK) and assembled in Malaysia, which marks pre-move stock. Date codes from about mid-2018 onward are likely the RFAB die. The PCN lists the affected orderables and the first ship date, but they were not seen. Forum posts note a sharp LM4562 price drop in early 2019 when new-die stock arrived.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved LM4562/LME49720 wafer fabrication from a 150 mm (6-inch) line to RFAB in Richardson, TX, on a newer process with a die-shrink redesign. The move revived the parts after the c.2015 'process-node end of life' notice. The TI E2E answer names the source fab as SFAB (Sherman, TX); a diyAudio thread is titled 'Fab moved from GB to US'. The PCN also covered other op-amps. Per TI E2E, LME49710 'remains without changes'.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. No published spec change and no old-vs-new measurement comparison was found. Claims of batch-to-batch sound differences are unverified forum folklore, and some predate the move.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same pinout, part number and datasheet limits. However, a die-shrink redesign could change unpublished behaviour (1/f or popcorn noise, RF susceptibility, start-up, overload recovery), and no old-vs-new data was found.

families.counterfeit_notes: The evidence comes from blogs and forums and was not re-verified on the web this pass. Marketplace DIP (NA) and TO-99 (HA) parts are frequently fake. Documented cases: a fake LME49710 (tinytransistors.net, 2022-09-24); a fake 'LME49720NA' (diyAudio thread 386852); a suspected fake LM4562NA (diyAudio thread 266368); and a Chinese 'LM4562NA' that JE6LVE measured at about 0.001% THD, against about 0.0006% for a genuine Akizuki-sourced part (je6lve.tom-system.com/archives/453). How to spot fakes: buy SOIC from authorized distributors; be suspicious of cheap TO-99 cans and National-logo NA parts; compare THD and quiescent current (12 mA max for the dual) with a known-good part; check that the marking and logo match the package era (National logo before 2011, TI after). Lot codes starting 'JR' indicate genuine Greenock-fab, Malaysia-assembled production (per diyAudio). A same-part-number die change (PCN 20180308002, 2018) is not counterfeiting, so a genuine new-production part may differ internally from vintage stock. The LM4562 vs LME49720 'voicing' claims are a separate matter: per TI E2E, both are the same silicon.

families.name: MC33078 / MC33079 (low-noise bipolar dual/quad)
families.tagline: Motorola's low-noise bipolar dual/quad (4.5 nV/√Hz, 16 MHz, 7 V/µs). Musiland used the MC33079 instead of the OP275 in its sound cards, and Soomal credited it with better treble detail.
families.technology: Bipolar, internally compensated, low-noise voltage-feedback op-amp. MC33078 is the dual and MC33079 the quad. The datasheets specify ±5 V to ±18 V supplies. The polarity of the input pair is unconfirmed. Motorola's SPICE library (MOTOR.LIB) tags the MC33078 model 'PNP Input', but that model is a generic Boyle template with an N-channel JFET input pair, so it is no evidence either way. onsemi lists input bias current as +300 nA, the same sign it gives the NPN-input NE5532, which hints at NPN. This is an unchecked inference. Three makers sell the part under the same number. onsemi's part is Motorola's original design. TI has made its own die since Oct 2004, and a TI engineer believes it is the same die as TI's LM833. ST's version is specified at 15 MHz rather than 16 MHz.
manufacturers: ON Semiconductor / onsemi (Motorola spin-off, 1999; ON-branded MC33078/D from Rev. 1, Feb 2001)
Texas Instruments (second source since Oct 2004; own die, shared with TI LM833 / RC4580 / new NE5532 per TI E2E)

Mirrors confirm these MC33078/D revisions: Rev. 1 (Feb 2001), Rev. 2 (Jan 2002), Rev. 4 (Sep 2003), Rev. 5 (Apr 2005), Rev. 8 (Jan 2009), Rev. 9 (Nov 2011) and Rev. 10 (Jul 2025, current). The NCV33078/NCV33079 automotive parts were added to the title by Rev. 9.

TI's datasheet SLLS633 was first issued in Oct 2004. Rev. A (Feb 2005) is titled MC33078, MC33079. Rev. C (Nov 2006) is still the current revision per ti.com. The enhanced-product datasheet is SLOS495. On E2E (thread 1443925), a TI engineer said the MC33078 and LM833 are believed to be the same die because their specs and graphs are identical. An SGS-Thomson-branded datasheet survives on studylib. ST's current datasheet ('Low noise dual operational amplifier', st.com) gives 4.5 nV/√Hz, 15 MHz GBP and 7 V/µs. The different GBP suggests ST's own die (unconfirmed).

reputation.summary: A budget low-noise bipolar dual/quad whose best-documented enthusiast praise comes from Soomal (China). Musiland dropped its usual OP275 for the MC33079 in the Monitor 03 US and 03 PS (PCM1798, 2011). It then used the part in the 06 MX (a TI part, 2013), the Monitor 10 (MC33079DG after an AK4490, 2016) and the 06 Plus (onsemi MC33079DG as a balanced I/V stage after an ES9028Q2M, 2017). Soomal said the 03 US had 'better treble detail' than the OP275-based 02 US. It heard the 03 PS as a little brighter, with finer resolution and better HF transients, but called the gain incremental. Both are whole-product judgements. In the 06 MX review Soomal also said the op-amp was not a top-tier Hi-Fi part. One EDAboard thread weighs it as a TL074 upgrade, and a guitar-pedal swap table says the TI MC33078 has 'very nice highs'. No ASR, Samuel Groner or Douglas Self measurements were found.
sonic_descriptors: better treble detail (Soomal, Monitor 03 US vs OP275-based 02 US; product-level)
a little brighter than the OP275-based 01 PS (Soomal, 03 PS; product-level)
finer resolution, clearly improved HF transients (Soomal, 03 PS; product-level)
'very nice highs' (guitar-pedal op-amp swap table, TI MC33078; folklore)
clean, slightly bright (op-amp-roller folklore; no source found)
typical_uses: I/V stage for differential current-output DACs (PCM1798 in Musiland Monitor 03 US / 03 PS / 06 MX)
balanced I/V stage after an ESS ES9028Q2M (Musiland Monitor 06 Plus, onsemi MC33079DG)
post-DAC filter/gain stage (Musiland Monitor 10 with AK4490)
headphone-amp gain stage (Soomal 'E-brand F-type' headphone amp, MC33078, 2010)
general consumer/pro audio preamps, active filters, guitar pedals, and op-amp rolling in place of TL07x/NE5532
caveats: Needs at least ±5 V (10 V total), so it does not suit low-voltage or USB-bus designs without a boost converter.
Bipolar input with about 300 nA typ bias current, so source impedances and DC paths matter.

TI's MC33078 is TI's own die. A TI engineer believes it is the same die as TI's LM833, and TI now says it shares one die with the NE5532, LM833 and RC4580 (E2E, 2026). TI and onsemi parts may therefore sound or measure differently despite the same number.
Several makers (onsemi, TI, ST, UTC) sell parts under the same number, and ST specifies 15 MHz GBW against 16 MHz for the others. No ON-vs-TI-vs-ST listening or measurement comparison was found.
All the Soomal praise is whole-product judgement, and Soomal itself called the MC33079 not a top-tier Hi-Fi part. Brand attribution in reviews is loose: Soomal called an onsemi MC33079DG 'Motorola'.

silicon_changes.when: Confirmed on TI E2E in 2026 (thread 1652528, around June 2026; Hackaday coverage 3 June 2026). It is linked to the NE5532 transition (SLOS075K, Dec 2025).
part_numbers_affected: MC33078 (TI orderables: MC33078D, MC33078DR, MC33078DGKR, MC33078DGKT, MC33078P, MC33078MDREP)
silicon_changes.identification: No MC33078-specific marker. TI's MC33078 datasheet is still SLLS633C (Nov 2006), and no PCN was found. The NE5532 change is marked by SLOS075K. onsemi, ST, UTC and Motorola-marked parts are unaffected.
silicon_changes.summary: TI E2E thread 1652528, 'NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 all now the same die', reports that TI has unified the four dies while keeping the part numbers. Search summaries describe it as the NE5532 moving onto the MC33078/RC4580-class die. In an earlier E2E thread (1443925), a TI engineer already believed the MC33078 and LM833 were the same die because their specs and graphs are identical. So the TI MC33078 may be the donor die rather than a changed part. Whether TI MC33078 silicon itself changed is unconfirmed. Headphonesty (July 2026) and Hackaday (June 2026) covered the consolidation.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Probably small or none for TI MC33078 if it was the donor die: SLLS633C still specifies 7 V/µs and 4.5 nV/√Hz. The large deltas (NE5532 slew 9→5 V/µs, input protection diodes removed, maximum supply ±22→±18 V) apply to the NE5532, not to MC33078 as documented.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: no MC33078 datasheet change or PCN was found, and the evidence points to NE5532 moving onto the MC33078/LM833 die. Re-qualify new TI lots only if a design depends on undocumented behaviour.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments / STMicroelectronics vs onsemi (Motorola design)
silicon_changes.when: TI since October 2004; ST since the SGS-Thomson era
silicon_changes.identification: Check the logo and top mark: TI's mark is reportedly 'M33078', and onsemi and ST parts carry their own logos. ST's datasheet specifies 15 MHz GBP where onsemi and TI specify 16 MHz.
silicon_changes.summary: Same part number, different silicon across vendors. TI's MC33078 is a TI second-source die, and a TI engineer believes it is identical to TI's LM833 (E2E 1443925). onsemi continues Motorola's original design. ST's version has a different GBP specification, which suggests an independent die. No measurement comparison between vendors was found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. The headline noise and slew figures match (4.5 nV/√Hz, 7 V/µs), but the internal circuits may differ, so reviews of one vendor's part may not transfer to another's.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: the pinout and headline specs match. Differences are second-order (GBW, possibly the input stage and protection).

families.counterfeit_notes: No MC33078/MC33079-specific counterfeit reports were found. Unbranded marketplace lots are the usual risk, for example eBay listings of '50/10 pcs MC33078DR SOP-8 MC33078D' with no maker stated. Alldatasheet gives the TI top mark as 'M33078' (not re-confirmed); the onsemi and ST markings were not captured. Folklore prefers Motorola-marked parts, so relabelled 'Motorola' vintage parts are plausible. Treat 'Motorola' parts with date codes well after 2001, when ON-branded MC33078/D Rev. 1 appeared, with suspicion. Buy from authorized distributors and check the logo, date code and marking.

families.name: MUSES01 / NJM5720 (New JRC / Nisshinbo J-FET-input dual, OFC lead frame)
families.tagline: New JRC's flagship JFET-input dual, the first op-amp with an OFC lead frame. Japanese listeners compare it to the OPA627 for its wide soundstage and smooth, refined treble.
families.technology: J-FET-input dual op-amp, DIP8 only. The 2025 Nisshinbo datasheet also lists 'Bipolar Technology' among its features, i.e. J-FET inputs on a bipolar process. PHILE WEB (2009-05-20) reported the part as the world's first to use a high-purity oxygen-free-copper (OFC) lead frame, with the package limited to DIP8 and low L/R crosstalk as a design goal. The datasheet gives 150 dB typ channel separation at 1 kHz. The 2025 English datasheet text says only 'unique material and assembled technology by skilled-craftwork' and does not name OFC. A 2024 factory-visit blog reports that Nisshinbo makes the lead frames in-house (not re-verified).

reputation.summary: One of the most highly regarded Japanese audio op-amps. Japanese enthusiasts often treat it as a domestic counterpart to the OPA627 and compare the two directly, for example in the e-earphone 'strongest op-amp' listening shoot-out, a mixi 'op-amp summit' (MUSES01 vs MUSES02 vs OPA627) and a 'MUSES01/02 vs OPA627BP' blog comparison. Listeners describe a wide soundstage and very smooth, refined, extended treble; one comparison notes slightly weak impact. Genre folklore is inconsistent: some describe MUSES01 as suited to classical music and MUSES02 to jazz vocals and pop, while others say the reverse. The rankings from these shoot-outs were not re-verified. No independent bench measurements (ASR, Samuel Groner) were found, so the praise rests on listening impressions.
sonic_descriptors: deep rather than punchy (slightly weak impact, per one comparison)
typical_uses: audio preamplifiers, active filters and line amplifiers (datasheet application list)
op-amp rolling in DACs, car audio and headphone amps with +/-9 V or higher rails
high-end Japanese DIY headphone amps and I/V or buffer stages
caveats: The vendor has confirmed NRND status (datasheet 20250321), and DigiKey and Mouser list it as NRND, so long-term supply is uncertain. The bipolar sibling MUSES02 is also NRND. MUSES03 and MUSES05 are reported discontinued (not re-verified).

The recommended supply is +/-9 V to +/-16 V. Single 5 V, +/-5 V or battery rails, as in many portable DAPs and headphone amps, are outside the recommended range. MUSES02, by contrast, is specified from +/-3.5 V.
Input bias current is 200 pA typ / 800 pA max at 25 C, high for a JFET-input part, and JFET bias current rises with temperature. Input offset is 5 mV max. Check DC coupling and high-impedance inputs.
The input common-mode range is only +/-8 V min (+/-9.5 V typ) on +/-15 V rails, which limits headroom in large-swing unity-gain buffers.
It is very expensive and widely counterfeited (see counterfeit_notes).
The soft OFC leads reportedly bend easily (not re-verified). Take care with repeated socket swaps.
DIP8 only; SOIC/SMD boards need an adapter.
The evidence is subjective listening only; no measurement shows it to be better.

families.counterfeit_notes:
Counterfeits are common and documented. The fakecomponents account on X has posted several fake MUSES01 listings on Japanese marketplaces (e.g. https://x.com/fakecomponents/status/895845393963012096, https://x.com/fakecomponents/status/1506883625526218760), and Japanese blogs (blog.luispc.com, ameblo) describe receiving fakes. Head-fi's saying is 'almost all [marketplace] sellers are selling fake MUSES'. Identification tells confirmed on the maimai-audio blog, for the MUSES01/02/03 goddess logo:
- Genuine marking is laser-engraved and slightly grey-white, flat with little relief.
- Fakes use pure white ink that you can feel, with thick or blurred characters.
- On genuine parts the goddess profile (forehead, nose, mouth, chin), the back-hair lines and the thin, evenly spaced wing slits stay sharp; on fakes they are filled in.
Unverified folklore: a misplaced pin-1 dot, and stiff non-copper leads instead of soft copper-coloured OFC leads.
Vendor-documented tell: MUSES01 is made only as a DIP8 dual, so any SMD, single-channel or 'MUSE01' single part on a DIP adapter is not genuine.
Maimai-audio also warns that print, logo position and lead finish vary by lot, so one difference alone does not prove a fake. Buy from Akizuki, Mouser, DigiKey or other authorised distributors. NRND status may make genuine stock scarcer.
alternatives: MUSES02 (bipolar-input sibling with the same OFC construction; specified from +/-3.5 V; also NRND)
MUSES8920 / MUSES8920A (lower-cost JFET-input MUSES; how the variants replace each other was not verified)
OPA2627 / OPA627 on an adapter (the traditional rival; OPA2627 is a true dual)
OPA1642 / OPA1656 (modern low-distortion JFET/CMOS-input duals)
MUSES03 (single-channel JFET flagship; reported discontinued, not verified)

families.technology: Bipolar-input dual op-amp. The datasheet title is "High Quality Audio, Bipolar Input, Dual Operational Amplifier" (JP: 2回路入り バイポーラ入力 高音質オペアンプ). reputation.summary: The bipolar partner to the JFET MUSES01, and a common premium DIP8 dual for op-amp rolling in Japanese, Chinese and English communities. It is also used as the front-end op-amp in portable amps: FiiO E12A and A5 (with LME49600), FiiO X7 AM2/AM5 modules, and VentureCraft SoundDroid Vantam. Listeners describe dynamics, a thick mid-bass and bass, 'richness' (芳醇) and high resolution (Japanese blogs). The Japanese rule of thumb is MUSES01 for vocals, MUSES02 for jazz and classical (unverified). Fosi Audio sells it as a replacement op-amp and lists it as compatible for the ZA3 and V3. Soomal (2017 FiiO A5 review) is more critical: MUSES02 'generally has good midrange stability, very steady, but somewhat dull (有些呆)'. The mid-bass vagueness in Soomal's 2015 Vantam review was attributed to the TPA6120A unbalanced output, not to MUSES02 vs LME49860. In an ASR phono-stage input-shorted noise test, the 33 EUR MUSES02 measured only about 0.3 dB better A-weighted noise than the 5 EUR OPA1656, i.e. about the same.
sonic_descriptors: thick, rich mid-bass and bass with punch (JP blogs)
high resolution / high information density (JP blogs)
warm, restrained (内敛) overall voicing in the Vantam (Soomal, applies to both MUSES02 and LME49860 settings)
critic: steady but somewhat dull / not lively midrange (Soomal, FiiO A5 review)
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DACs and amplifiers (Fosi ZA3 / V3 list it as compatible)
Portable headphone amps: FiiO E12A and A5 (MUSES02 + LME49600, per Soomal)
FiiO X7 amp modules AM2 (MUSES02 + BUF634) and AM5 (MUSES02 + TPA6120A2), per a review aggregation
VentureCraft SoundDroid Vantam (MUSES02 or LME49860 front end, per Soomal)
Audio preamplifiers, active filters, line amplifiers (datasheet application list)
Upgrade from NJM4580 / NE5532 in Japanese DIY
caveats: Counterfeits and remarked parts are widely reported in marketplace listings (community reports)
MUSES02D is a maintenance product (保守品) per the Nisshinbo JP datasheet of 2025-03-19; Nisshinbo says such parts will be discontinued in the near future and are not for new designs
Bipolar input with 100 nA typ (500 nA max) bias current, so DC offset can rise with high source impedances or in DC-coupled designs
Minimum supply is ±3.5 V, which is marginal on low-voltage single-rail gear
Datasheet THD is specified at AV=+10 / 5 Vrms / 2 kΩ, not directly comparable to LME49860 / OPA1612 figures
Measured noise advantage over far cheaper parts is small (ASR: ~0.3 dB A-weighted vs OPA1656 in one phono stage)
Voicing is subjective and polarising: Soomal finds the midrange steady but dull
DIP8 only, with no SMD option
Sonic descriptors are subjective listening impressions, not measurements

families.counterfeit_notes: Community reports (low-to-medium confidence), consistent across English, Japanese and Chinese sources: counterfeits and remarked parts are common on AliExpress, eBay, Amazon JP and Yahoo Auctions. Checks: (1) genuine parts have an OFC lead frame, so the leads are soft and very pliable and copper-toned, while fakes have stiff plated leads (Head-Fi opamp thread p.307); (2) the round pin-1 indent should sit right at pin 1, and fakes often show a flat stamped circle (Head-Fi); (3) genuine logo is described as finely detailed and sharp, while fakes use coarse or white-ink printing. An AliExpress SEO article claims raised, laser-like lettering marks fakes, which contradicts other reports; treat marking texture as unreliable. Caveat from maimai-audio: print, logo position, back finish and lead finish vary legitimately by lot and era (NJR vs Nisshinbo branding), so variation alone is not proof. Pricing: the '$3–5 genuine' figure circulating in SEO articles is not supported; the ASR test cites 33 EUR for a MUSES02 and a diyAudio thread (Apr 2023) cites about $44 at Mouser. Treat listings far below authorized-distributor prices (Mouser, DigiKey, Akizuki, Marutsu, Eleshop) as suspect.

families.name: MUSES05 (J-FET single, two-chip MUSES flagship, DFN12-CA8)
families.tagline: The current MUSES flagship: a two-chip JFET single on an oxygen-free copper frame, which some Head-Fi rollers rank among the most resolving op-amps they have tried.
families.technology: J-FET input, single channel. Two-chip construction puts the input stage and the output stage on separate dies to reduce interference between them (NJR 2021-06-23 release; EE Times Japan 2021-06-24). A Japanese press summary says a 'full-balance differential amplifier circuit' (フルバランス型差動増幅回路) improves response, dynamic range and distortion; the exact source page was not pinned. Package is DFN12-CA8 (ESON12-CA8) with an exposed pad and an oxygen-free copper (OFC) frame, which the vendor says gives both sound quality and heat dissipation. The datasheet cites 'advanced circuit design and special material and assembly technology'. Headline specs almost match the MUSES03 datasheet Ver.4.2: 7.5 nV/rtHz, 5 pA, 12 MHz, 5.8 mA and +/-3.5 to +/-18 V are the same. The visible headline difference is slew rate, 40 V/us against 35 V/us.
manufacturers: New Japan Radio Co., Ltd. (NJR / New JRC) - originator
Nisshinbo Micro Devices Inc. (successor to NJR)

reputation.summary: NJR/Nisshinbo position it as the MUSES op-amp with the highest sound quality. EE Times Japan headlined it as a new flagship of sound-first op-amps made 'regardless of productivity' (生産性度外視). PHILE WEB's 2021 listening report says it shows left-right staging and renders three-dimensional depth 'even more deeply'. On Head-Fi's Opamp thread (pages 490-497), a roller calls it roughly twice as fast as MUSES03 and a refinement of the MUSES sound, with more speed, resolution, air and reverb but less vocal body. The same roller ranks it with the Burson V7 Vivid as the most resolving parts tried, and says MUSES03 still wins on some tracks because of its physicality and weight. That poster adds that people who dislike MUSES03 will probably dislike MUSES05 too. Japanese DIY blogs use it in Quad405-clone op-amp swaps, T.b.sound amp builds, KORG HA-K headphone amps and DUO dual adapters. One Quad405-clone comparison could not clearly tell MUSES03D and MUSES05 apart. No independent measurements (ASR, diyAudio, Samuel Groner) were found.
sonic_descriptors: fast (about 2x MUSES03 per the same poster)
sharp / tight, sharper focus and microdynamics
airy, more reverb/ambience; less body than MUSES03
left-right staging with deeper 3D depth (PHILE WEB)
typical_uses: I/V converters after DACs (datasheet application)
preamplifiers / line amplifiers
active filters
headphone amplifiers
op-amp rolling via DIP8 conversion modules or kits (Akizuki g117651 / g117650) or two on a DUO-style dual adapter
caveats: SMD-only DFN12-CA8 package. Socket rolling needs a DIP8 conversion module, and results then depend on the adapter (community practice; no stability data found).
It is a single, so a dual-op-amp socket needs two parts on an adapter such as the MUSES05 DUO.
5.8 mA typ supply current matters in battery gear.

Supply has been intermittent: customer-only allocation in 2021, open-market sale apparently only from about December 2022, then a production suspension over material availability before the restart. Resellers have listed it as discontinued (廃版 / 生産終了品).
Praise comes from a few listeners and is subjective. At least one blogger could not reliably tell it from MUSES03D, and its headline datasheet specs are nearly identical to MUSES03.
No independent THD or noise measurements were located.

families.counterfeit_notes: No MUSES05-specific counterfeit reports were found. new_western_elec's counterfeit survey covers DIP parts (OPA2604, OPA627, MUSES01), not MUSES05. The SMD DFN12-CA8 package is harder to fake convincingly than the DIP8 MUSES01, MUSES02, MUSES8820 and MUSES8920. The practical risk is DIP-converted or dualised modules resold on Yahoo Auctions, Yahoo Flea Market and Mercari, often labelled 廃版 or 生産終了品 (discontinued) at high prices, where the chip cannot be inspected. Buy bare MUSES05-TE3 from authorised channels (Mouser, DigiKey, Farnell/element14), or from Akizuki (bare chip g117512, kit g117650 or finished module g117651), and check that the DFN marking and date code look consistent.

reputation.summary: In Japanese, Chinese and English rolling communities MUSES8920 is called the 'budget MUSES01' (Head-Fi) and is a common cheap JFET upgrade for NE5532/NJM4580 sockets. Japanese listeners describe it as clean, dry and high-resolution with no grain, keeping some of OPA2604's softness with a thinner line and a wider stage. A diyAudio I/V comparison found only subtle gains over NE5532: a little more clarity and detail, the same soundstage. Soomal (CN) called its sound thick and restrained (厚重，内敛) but said MUSES-equipped DACs it had heard were distinctive rather than outstanding. Commercial users include the Shanling M2 DAP (post-DAC low-pass filter), VentureCraft Vantam (balanced headphone output), TEAC AX-505 and Magnetar UDP800. In new_western_elec's 2025 ranking it placed above MUSES8820 and OPA2604 but below Nisshinbo's NL8802/NL8902. A Head-Fi round-up measured it; the figures were not captured.
sonic_descriptors: slightly clearer and more detailed than NE5532, differences subtle (diyAudio, I/V)
OPA2604-like softness, thinner line, wider soundstage (JP, kakaku)
a bit rounded off and cautious at the bass/treble extremes (Head-Fi)
smoother with more low-end thickness than MUSES8820 (JP search summary, source page unclear)
typical_uses: op-amp rolling in DACs, CD players and headphone amps (replacing NE5532/NJM4580/OPA2604)
DAC I/V conversion (J-FET input, pA bias current)
DAC post-filter / low-pass and line output stages (e.g. Shanling M2 LPF, Magnetar UDP800 analog stage)
balanced headphone output in portable gear (VentureCraft Vantam: two MUSES8920; the unbalanced output uses TPA6120A)
integrated amplifier signal stages (TEAC AX-505)
caveats: Needs at least +/-3.5 V supply, so it is unsuited to very low-voltage rails. The maximum operating supply is +/-16 V for MUSES8920 and +/-17 V for MUSES8920A. JRC's low-voltage MUSES is MUSES8832 (2014).

MUSES8920D (DIP8) is discontinued. The replacement MUSES8920A is surface-mount only (AD DIP8 never released), so socketed gear needs an SOP8-to-DIP8 adapter such as Akizuki's MUSES8920AE DIP module kit.

Nisshinbo says 8920A is electrically and sonically equivalent. new_western_elec (Nov 2025) heard deeper sub-bass, a slightly thinner bass line, less treble extension and 'something catching' vs the old 8920D, and suggested unit variation. This is one listener, and the SMD-on-adapter vs DIP comparison is a likely confound.
Fake MUSES8920D parts have been reported (new_western_elec, Nov 2023). Buy from authorised channels.
Some listeners find it restrained or cautious at the frequency extremes. Soomal found MUSES-based DACs characterful but not outstanding overall.
In some circuits the gain over NE5532 is small (diyAudio I/V comparison).

families.counterfeit_notes: new_western_elec reported in November 2023 that fake MUSES8920D parts were circulating, per a search summary that names AliExpress and Mercari. The identifying features in that post were not captured. AliExpress still lists 'NEW GENUINE ORIGINAL' MUSES8920D DIP8 lots years after end of production. Other documented MUSES fakes (maimai-audio, fakecomponents on X, rarirureluis) are MUSES01/02, with thin, irregular numerals, lighter print instead of laser etching and wrong JRC logo details. Practical checks: (1) Buy from authorised channels (Mouser, DigiKey, Akizuki, eleshop, Seiwa, Profusion). (2) Treat cheap 'new' MUSES8920D as suspect, since production has ended. (3) A bare DIP8 chip marked 'MUSES8920A' is suspect, because MUSES8920AD was never released and legitimate DIP-form 8920A items are adapter boards (inference). (4) Compare the marking font, logo and laser etch against genuine JRC-era parts under magnification.

families.name: NE5532 / NE5532A / SA5532 / SE5532 (dual low-noise bipolar; incl. NJM5532, KA5532, BA15532, RC5532)
families.tagline: The 1979 Signetics dual that became the pro-audio benchmark: 5 nV/rtHz, 600 ohm drive, cheap. Douglas Self's reference part; Soomal calls it the 'king of op-amps'.
families.technology: Bipolar, internally compensated (unity-gain stable) dual; the dual version of the NE5534 core. Legacy parts (Signetics/Philips, onsemi, TI up to SLOS075J) use an NPN input pair with anti-parallel input-protection diodes and a class-AB output specified into 600 ohm. TI's current die (documented from SLOS075K, Dec 2025) is a redesign on a newer process after the move from SFAB Sherman (150 mm) to RFAB Richardson. A TI E2E thread (Jun 2026) says NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 now share one die, and summaries describe it as RC4580-derived with no input diodes. Input-stage polarity is disputed: Gearspace says PNP, the E2E-thread summary says NPN.

reputation.summary: The reference pro-audio op-amp since 1979 and the stock part that op-amp rolls are judged against. Douglas Self uses it as the benchmark in Small Signal Audio Design and argues bad reports come from misuse. NwAvGuy's 2011 measurements put it alongside far pricier parts. Soomal (China) calls it '号称运放之皇' ('reputed king of op-amps') and uses it as a benchmark tier ('4558 < 5532/4580'). Japanese reviewer nabe treats it as the baseline 'normal audio op-amp' (rank B). Vintage Signetics and Philips stock has a following in Japan and China, and junker-life preferred Signetics/Philips by ear over TI and JRC. These are subjective reports.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / clean, transparent at line level when used correctly (Self)
soft, warm mid-bass with slower transients and less treble resolution than modern parts (Soomal RNHP review)
retro / vintage flavour ('复古的味道', Soomal)
flat or plain next to boutique parts (op-amp rollers)
typical_uses: mixing consoles and pro line stages driving 600 ohm
CD player and DAC I/V and output stages
preamps, tone controls, active crossovers
powered speakers (e.g. Soomal's 鹂之声 启明星)
headphone amps (with or without buffers)
MM phono and RIAA stages
caveats: TI parts on the new die (documented from SLOS075K, Dec 2025, though forums say shipments began earlier) are rated 5 V/us slew and ±18 V absolute maximum, and the 600 ohm drive specs are gone. Designs on ±18 to ±22 V rails can be overstressed. Production boards failed QA after the change (Scott Dorsey, via Headphonesty).
The new TI die reportedly drops the input-protection diodes and halves HBM ESD (2 kV to 1 kV).
Needs split rails of at least about ±5 V. The output is not rail-to-rail (common-mode range ±12 V on ±15 V).
Quiescent current is several mA per package, so it runs warm in dense or small builds.
Bipolar input bias current (hundreds of nA) causes DC offset with high source impedance. It is not a drop-in for FET-input sockets that rely on low bias current.
Legacy parts have anti-parallel input-protection diodes, so they are unsuitable as comparators or with large differential inputs.
Brands differ. Douglas Self reportedly found TI parts noisier with higher HF THD than Fairchild/onsemi (forum report, not primary-source verified). JRC NJM5532 is described as looser.
Counterfeit and remarked 'NOS Signetics/Philips' parts are common on marketplaces.

silicon_changes.when: Process/fab PCN reportedly dated Nov 15, 2023 (diyAudio); production moved from SFAB Sherman (150 mm) to RFAB Richardson around 2024 (Gearspace: 'K version – 2024>'); datasheet Rev K Dec 2025; datasheet PCN 20260429001 Apr 30, 2026 (first ship Jul 29, 2026)
silicon_changes.identification: A SLOS075K or later datasheet means the new die; SLOS075J or earlier means the legacy die. Orderable part numbers are unchanged, and no date-code cutover has been published. Legacy parts have back-to-back diodes across the inputs and the new die reportedly has none, so an unpowered diode check between IN+ and IN- can separate them (E2E-thread summary). A bench test also works: slew about 5 V/us on the new die versus 9 V/us on the legacy die. TI E2E thread 1294367 (late 2023) asks for the PCN on an NE5532DR 'symbolization format' (marking) change, which may be a visual clue (unconfirmed). The PCN number for the process change has not been identified. Candidates are the Nov 15, 2023 PCN (number not captured), 20240529002, 20240806004, 20241217004, 20250129000 and 20250730004; none is confirmed to list NE5532.
silicon_changes.summary: TI replaced the NE5532/NE5532A/SA5532/SA5532A silicon with a redesign on a newer process in RFAB, without changing the part numbers. A TI E2E thread says NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 are now the same die, and summaries describe it as RC4580-derived. Hackaday reports that the process-change notice gave impact 'None'. The datasheet was updated only in Dec 2025 (Rev K), and the datasheet PCN followed in Apr 2026. Hackaday calls the result incompatible even with the original Signetics NE5532.

spec_deltas.after: removed (Headphonesty, Mithat, E2E thread); the Rev K description text reportedly still mentions them

spec_deltas.parameter: Equivalent input noise, CMRR, DC AVD

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Full-power bandwidth at 10 V peak falls from about 143 kHz to about 80 kHz (computed from the slew rate), which leaves less HF THD margin at high output level. Drive into 600 ohm and other heavy loads is no longer guaranteed. Consoles and powered speakers on ±18 to ±22 V (often unregulated) rails can exceed the new absolute maximum. Without the input diodes, circuits that relied on them for differential-input clamping lose that protection. The higher GBW and different input stage can change stability and HF behaviour in legacy layouts. Production boards failed QA after the TI parts were swapped in (Scott Dorsey, via Headphonesty).
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: high – same part number but lower voltage rating, slower slew, halved ESD, no input diodes and deleted load-drive guarantees; not a drop-in for legacy ±18 to ±22 V or 600 ohm designs

families.counterfeit_notes: Remarked fakes are common on marketplaces, especially 'NOS Signetics/Philips' parts (vintage stock sells for over 100 RMB in China, which motivates relabelling). Elektroda shows a fake NE5532 decapped next to a genuine one (https://www.elektroda.com/rtvforum/topic3386559.html), and TI E2E has an 'NE5532: Genuine or fake?' thread (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1474706/ne5532-genuine-or-fake). Discovery notes also mention relabelled LM741-class dies (diyAudio fake-AD797/LM741 thread). To spot fakes: a genuine 5532 draws several mA per package, far above LM358/741-class parts. It should drive 600 ohm cleanly and slew about 9 V/us (legacy) or 5 V/us (new TI). Compare the marking font and logo against known date codes, and buy from authorized distributors. A genuine new TI part now slews at only 5 V/us and has no input diodes, so neither test alone proves a fake.

families.name: NE5534 / NE5534A / SA5534 / SE5534 (incl. NJM5534) - single low-noise decompensated bipolar
families.tagline: Signetics' 1979 low-noise decompensated single and the 5532's forerunner: about 3.5 nV/rtHz, 10 MHz and 600-ohm drive. A staple of consoles, CD/DAC stages and MM/mic preamps.
families.technology: Bipolar single op amp, decompensated: internally compensated for gains of about 3 or more. For unity or low gain, an external capacitor goes between COMP and COMP/BAL (pins 5 and 8). The TI datasheet headline figures of 13 V/us and 10 MHz UGBW were confirmed by web search. onsemi NE5534/D carries the Signetics-derived wording ('Compared to other operational amplifiers such as TL083...'). Dave Jones (EEVblog 1752) notes that the TI NE5532 and NE5534 'haven't always been exactly the same design'.

reputation.summary: The single-channel, decompensated forerunner of the NE5532. It is lower in noise than the 5532 and drives 600-ohm loads. Douglas Self covers it alongside the 5532 in his books, and it is widely used in MM phono, mic and line stages of consoles, CD players, DAC filter stages and ADC drivers (the AKM AK5383 reference circuit uses NJM5534). Dave Jones (EEVblog) treats it as a low-noise audio default. diyAudio posters (not re-verified) say it sounds good when correctly compensated, and it is a common baseline that upgrades such as the OPA627 are compared against. Soomal (China) calls the TI NE5534 fitted in the Creative AE-9 clearly lower grade than the LM49710 it replaced. It also notes Matrix using the 'old-flavour' NE5534 in the HPA-2 Classic low-pass filter. In Japan, vintage Signetics/Philips NOS parts have a following, and bloggers rank them above TI and JRC versions (anecdotal).
sonic_descriptors: neutral / clean when properly compensated (diyAudio, anecdotal)
softer and less 'hard' than AD797/OPA1611, but less dynamic and resolving (Soomal, AE-9 op-amp roll)
vintage Signetics/Philips NOS described as an upgrade over TI/JRC (Japanese blogs, anecdotal)
typical_uses: MM phono and microphone preamps
mixing-console line and mic stages
CD-player / DAC I/V and low-pass filter stages (e.g. Matrix M-Stage HPA-2 Classic LPF)
ADC input drivers (AKM AK5383 reference circuit uses NJM5534)
socketed op-amp positions in sound cards (Creative AE-9 ships TI NE5534)
caveats: Decompensated: in a unity-gain or low-gain socket it needs the external COMP to COMP/BAL capacitor. Dropping it into a unity-gain buffer position can oscillate.
Second-source parts (Signetics/Philips, TI, onsemi, JRC) are separate vendor products. Differences in compensation margin are community reports only, so verify stability when swapping brands.
The TI NE5532 and NE5534 are not guaranteed identical designs (EEVblog 1752). Don't assume 5532 behaviour carries over to the 5534, or the reverse.
TI NE5534AD (SOIC tube) is reported EOL; TI points to NE5534ADRG4. Distributors have at times shown NE5534 variants as obsolete although TI lists them as active.

TI's NE5532 redesign (PCN20231114002.1: abs-max supply +/-22 V to +/-18 V, ESD 2 kV to 1 kV) does NOT apply to the NE5534 as of Sep 2026. SLOS070D (Nov 2014) is still current. Re-check for any SLOS070E or NE5534 PCN.
JRC NJM5534D/M are obsolete; the current JRC part is NJM5534DD.

families.counterfeit_notes: Marketplaces sell 'Signetics / former Philips NE5534N' NOS (e.g. eBay listings); remarked fakes are reported in discovery notes but not independently verified. Japanese blogs say NOS NE5534 sells above NE5532, which would make relabelling attractive (anecdotal). Genuine OEM house-numbered Signetics NE5534s also exist (HP custom part numbers, per EEVblog), so an odd marking is not proof of a fake. Precautions: be sceptical of large 'NOS Signetics' lots, check that the marking style and date code fit the claimed era, and buy current production (TI NE5534P/NE5534AP/ADRG4, onsemi, NJM5534DD) from authorised distributors. Bench-check noise and stability: a decompensated part at unity gain without the cap may oscillate, which can mask other differences.

families.name: NJM4580 / JRC4580 (incl. TI RC4580) (dual audio bipolar)
families.tagline: Japan's cheap 'standard audio op-amp' in countless sound cards, CD players and DACs; praised for a neutral, high-resolution 'plain as water' sound, rated above NE5532 by Soomal.
families.technology: Bipolar dual op-amp in the standard dual pinout (pin-compatible with 4558/5532-type duals), optimised for audio ('specially designed for improving tone control'): low noise, 15 MHz GBW, high output current, low THD, ±2 V minimum supply. NJM4580 input stage is PNP according to JP hobby notes and two NJR-labelled SPICE macromodels (medium confidence; datasheet equivalent circuit not read). TI RC4580 is a separate TI-made part whose input polarity is contested: Headphonesty says the RC4580-die NE5532 went from a PNP to an NPN input stage, while Rich Cabot and diyAudio posters describe the RC4580-die NE5532 as PNP-input. The classic NE5532 is commonly documented with an NPN input pair, so Headphonesty's direction may be reversed (inference, not checked this pass).

reputation.summary: The default 'standard audio op-amp' in Japanese and Chinese consumer audio. Soomal found the JRC4580 in many mid- and high-end sound cards, active speakers, headphone amps and DACs, calling it 'not top-tier but better than the so-called king of op-amps NE5532' and describing it as high-resolution and neutral or plain ('平白如水'), adaptable but characterless, unlike the warm OP275. Japanese hobby sources call it the standard audio op-amp: fast and smooth with low residual noise, mellow and easy to listen to, though some find it overly smooth or veiled. Opinion is not uniform: nabe.adiary's CMoy comparison puts NJM4580 in C rank below NE5532 (B); a Chinese PC-audio primer calls it NE5532-like and average; English forums say it is chosen for price rather than performance, and some call it 'somewhat edgy and lacking detail'. Its ±2 V minimum supply makes it popular for USB-powered DIY; a 2012 srad.jp commenter ran the '50-yen NJM4580DD' straight from USB power.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / plain ('平白如水', '音色中性平淡' - Soomal)
high resolution ('解析力出色', '解析力高' - Soomal)
adaptable but characterless ('对声音的适应性强，但缺乏特点' - Soomal)
fast and smooth, low residual noise (JP hobby notes)
mellow and easy listening; to some, overly smooth or veiled (JP notes on NJM4580DD)
relatively flat with good HF extension (JP repair-shop note)
similar to NE5532, average (Chinese PC-audio primer, per search summary)
'somewhat edgy and lacking detail' (minority English-forum view)
typical_uses: Sound-card analog outputs (Soomal: TerraTec DMX 6Fire LT; TempoTec Hifier Fantasia / Variations / Sonata / X-Fi Rhapsody; Musiland Moli; 傲王 SQ717; AUDIOPROBE SPARTAN CUE 110)
Sound-card recording input gain stage (Musiland X-Sword II main card, per Soomal)
Active speakers (Musiland C260 / C280 / N66II)
Headphone amps and DACs (Musiland HP10; TempoTec Fantasia DAII Plus unbalanced output)
Japanese CD players and AV gear (ONKYO / DENON / PIONEER per JP repair-shop notes)
DIY USB-powered DAC and headphone-amp stages (±2 V minimum supply)
Preamp, tone-control, active-filter and headphone-amp stages (datasheet target applications)
caveats: Not a high-end part. Soomal calls it good but not top-tier and characterless, nabe.adiary ranks it below NE5532, and a Chinese primer calls it average. The 'better than NE5532' verdict comes from one reviewer (Soomal).
Soomal says it is often confused with the far cheaper, pin-compatible JRC4558.
Nisshinbo gives no input noise current and only an RIAA-weighted noise figure (RS=2.2 kΩ, 30 kHz LPF); nV/√Hz is only a graph.
Nisshinbo's 20250303 datasheet marks NJM4580D (DIP8) and NJM4580L (SIP8) NRND. The D-rank DIP (NJM4580DD / D-D) is not addressed separately, and future DIP rolling stock may need SMD-to-DIP adapters.
TI RC4580 is a different part (GBW 12 vs 15 MHz). The reputation was earned by the JRC part; TI's NE5532, LM833 and MC33078 now reportedly use the RC4580 die.
The datasheet claims headphone-amp suitability (±13.5 V typ into 2 kΩ at ±15 V), but low-impedance headphones benefit from a buffer (general practice, not measured here).
The '50 yen' price comes from a 2012 comment; current prices were not checked.

silicon_changes.identification: NE5532/NE5532A: SLOS075K (December 2025) documents the new silicon; SLOS075J (January 2015) and earlier describe the legacy die. RC4580 has no documented marker: its datasheet went to SLOS412E in November 2024 (change list not captured). Check TI PCN device lists and lot/date codes from 2024 onward.
silicon_changes.summary: A TI E2E thread titled 'NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 all now the same die' confirms the consolidation. Hackaday reports Rich Cabot (Audio Precision co-founder) identifying the RC4580 die in the new NE5532 ('they just relabeled a 4580'). Headphonesty reports field failures on boards using ±22 V-class rails, removal of the NE5532's input protection diodes and halved HBM ESD; the E2E summary notes the classic NE5532 has back-to-back input diodes whereas the RC4580 does not. For RC4580 buyers this is the donor design, so little change is expected; the hazard is for NE5532/LM833/MC33078 users.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: No RC4580-specific audio change is documented. A post-2024 TI NE5532, LM833 or MC33078 now behaves like an RC4580-class part (5 V/µs, ±18 V max, no input diodes), not like the classic 5532.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low for RC4580 (it is the donor die; headline specs unchanged), but its own post-migration change list is unknown; high for NE5532/LM833 users on legacy ±18 to ±22 V rails or relying on input diodes.

families.counterfeit_notes: Soomal warns that JRC4580 is often confused with the far cheaper, pin-compatible JRC4558. Relabelling 4558s as 4580s is therefore the plausible main risk, but no documented teardown or measurement case was found, and the discovery claim that 'JRC4580' clones/remarks are common was not confirmed (low confidence). Buy from authorised channels (Mouser, RS, Marutsu, Akizuki, Keisei, Digi-Key). Check that the logo (JRC/NJR/Nisshinbo), laser-marking font and date codes are consistent. Distrust cheap 'NOS' DIP lots, since the DIP NJM4580D is NRND and supply will tighten. D-rank parts appear as 'NJM4580DD' in distributor listings and 'NJM4580D-D' in the 2025 datasheet. Quick bench check: GBW about 15 MHz and slew about 5 V/µs; 4558-class parts are much slower. TI RC4580 is a legitimate but different die (12 MHz GBW).

families.name: OPA1611 / OPA1612 (TI SoundPlus bipolar-input, 1.1 nV/√Hz single/dual)
families.tagline: TI's 1.1 nV/√Hz bipolar audio op-amp with −136 dB THD+N at 1 kHz. It is widely used for I/V conversion and buffering in modern DACs, DAPs and Hi-Fi phones.
families.technology: Bipolar-input, voltage-feedback op-amp, unity-gain stable. The output is rail-to-rail (within 0.6 V at 2 kΩ, 0.2 V at 10 kΩ). The inputs have back-to-back differential clamp diodes. Copper leadframe (SBOS450C §7.3.1). Rev A (Aug 2009) and Rev B (Jul 2011) front pages carry 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding and the title 'High-Performance Bipolar-Input AUDIO OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'; web search shows this in the mirror titles. Rev C (Aug 2014) is titled 'OPA161x SoundPlus™'. TI's current parametric listing still tags the part 'Burr-Brown™ Audio'. The OPA1611 comes in SOIC-8 (D) only. The OPA1612 comes in SOIC-8 (D) or SON-8 3×3 mm (DRG), which TI's parametric table calls WSON. No DIP package appears in the datasheet or the orderable addendum.

reputation.summary: Its measured noise and distortion are exceptional (1.1 nV/√Hz, −136 dB THD+N), and measurement-oriented users treat it as essentially transparent (discovery note). In audioXpress 'Modern Op-Amp Distortion Tests, Part 1' (author not confirmed here), the OPA1612 showed less distortion than the NE5532 with shunt feedback and much less as a voltage follower, but about the same with series feedback. Soomal teardowns show it spreading through Chinese Hi-Fi phones and DAPs from 2014: FiiO X5, Meizu MX4 Pro, vivo X5 Max, Xiaomi Note and Smartisan T2. In 2022 Soomal said a very large share of recent products use the OPA1612 for I/V conversion. Japanese hobbyists call it a neutral 'reference sound' all-rounder (discovery note, not verified). The subjective camp is split. Soomal found it 'hard, not pleasing' (偏硬，不够讨喜) in a 2020 AE-9 op-amp swap, though with better dynamics and resolution than the NE5534. In 2016 Soomal argued that bipolar parts like the OPA1612 sound worse on average than DiFET types, and that passage mislabels the OPA1612 as 'Bipolar FET'.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / 'reference sound' (JP, maimai-audio; discovery note, unverified)
flat, not genre-dependent (JP owners; discovery note, unverified)
musical, delicate and warm (OPA1611; Audiogon thread per discovery note; low confidence)
hard / 偏硬, not pleasing (Soomal 2020, AE-9 op-amp swap, where it is written 'OP1611')
better dynamics and resolution than NE5534 (same Soomal 2020 passage)
average sound worse than DiFET types (Soomal 2016, 901 player / MINIBOX review)
typical_uses: DAC I/V conversion: Sabaj A20d (2022), with three OPA1612 for I/V and separate op-amps marked '2149U' doing the LPF, and Topping DX7 Pro (both per Soomal 2022)
Output LPF in DAPs (SoundAware MR1 with dual CS4398, per Soomal 2017)

Post-I/V amplifier or buffer in Hi-Fi phones and DAPs: Meizu MX4 Pro (2014), vivo X5 Max (2014), Xiaomi Note (2015, after ADA4896 I/V), Smartisan T2 (2016, two OPA1612 replacing one OPA2604), FiiO X5 (2014, with an LMH6643 buffer), all per Soomal
Input or error amplifier in VFA-CFA composite headphone amps with TPA6120 or THS6012 (e.g. the PWieland/SCAM project)
Professional audio, microphone preamps, mixing consoles, broadcast gear, audio test equipment and A/V receivers (TI's listed applications)
Op-amp rolling via DIP-8 adapter boards
caveats: Current noise is fairly high (1.7 pA/√Hz @1 kHz). With source or feedback networks of 10 kΩ or more it loses its noise advantage over FET-input parts, as a JP hobbyist's 2026 design notes (indare/pcb_work) also found.
The input common-mode range stops 2 V from each rail, so G = +1 buffers clip early on low supplies.
The back-to-back input diodes can conduct on fast edges in low-gain or G = +1 circuits. TI says to limit input current to 10 mA.
At low gain, capacitive loads reduce phase margin and can cause peaking or oscillation; TI suggests about 50 Ω series isolation (§8.4). Layout and decoupling on DIP adapters matter.
Iq is 3.6 mA per channel and θJA of SOIC-8 is 150 °C/W. TI says soldering rather than socketing reduces temperature rise.
It comes only in SOIC or SON, so every 'DIP' part is an adapter board. Relabelled TL082 fakes are documented (diyAudio 332536).
The audioXpress advantage over the NE5532 depends on topology: it is clear for shunt feedback and followers, and about equal with series feedback.
The subjective descriptors conflict with each other, and no controlled listening test was verified.

revision_history.changes: Initial release. The date comes from the 'JULY 2009' origin line in later headers. No copy was found, and the original→A changes are not recorded in Rev C.

The header is confirmed by web mirrors (Reichelt, BDTIC and alldatasheet 311775, per search summaries). The front page carries 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding, the title 'High-Performance Bipolar-Input AUDIO OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS' and the 'IN- Pre-Output Driver' layout; the alldatasheet copy has 21 pages. The Rev C log does not record what changed from the original.

The header is confirmed by the Octopart 21221010 copy (web search summary). A→B, per the Rev C change log: revised Features list; updated front-page figure; added a max spec for input voltage noise density at 1 kHz (1.5 nV/√Hz); corrected a typo in EC footnote 1; revised Figures 4, 7, 9, 11, 15 and 29; revised the Electrical Overstress section; revised the table in Figure 34. No absolute-max, pinout or silicon change is indicated. 'Burr-Brown Audio' branding is retained.

B→C: new TI datasheet format; added the SON-8 (DRG) package (IB max ±300 nA for DRG); renamed SO to SOIC; added the front-page curve; added a block-diagram title; replaced the Package Information table with the addendum. The title became 'OPA161x SoundPlus™'. Still current in Sep 2026 per web search: gpn/OPA1612 serves SBOS450C and no SBOS450D was found. TI refreshed only the addendum and T&R pages, dated 10-Nov-2025.

families.counterfeit_notes: Confirmed by web search in diyAudio thread 332536 ('Fake OPA1612 from China'): a buyer bought 10 'OPA1612' from a Chinese eBay seller for €6.80 in total. Under the microscope they turned out to be relabelled TL082 JFET dies, identified by the cross-shaped 'butterfly' FET input devices, not bipolar OPA1612 dies. A TI E2E thread, 'OPA1612 - Fake chips?' (532783), exists; its content was not seen. diyAudio thread 399994 ('OPA1612 from Aliexpress, no counterfeit but why so cheap?') reports cheap AliExpress parts that decapped as genuine OPA1612 dies, so cheap does not always mean fake. The roughly 150 nA input bias reported there (discovery note) is inside the ±250 nA max. Screening tips from the datasheet: (1) TI lists only SOIC-8 (D) and, for the OPA1612, SON-8 (DRG), so a DIP-8 body marked OPA161x is not a TI package. (2) The genuine SOIC top mark is 'OPA' over '1611A' or '1612A', and the DRG mark is 'OVII'. (3) Iq should be about 3.6 mA per channel, 4.5 mA max. (4) Input bias should be tens of nA; pA-level bias points to a JFET relabel. (5) Noise should be about 1.1 nV/√Hz, so a relabelled TL08x is roughly ten times noisier. Buy from TI or authorised distributors.

families.name: OPA604 / OPA2604 (Burr-Brown FET-input, low-distortion audio op-amp)
families.tagline: Burr-Brown's early-90s FET-input audio op-amp with on-chip distortion rejection and ±24 V rails; the warm, "tube-like" (胆味) classic of CD-player, sound-card and phone Hi-Fi.
families.technology: FET-input voltage-feedback op-amp. The block diagram shows 'Distortion Rejection Circuitry' and an 'Output Stage', both marked 'Patents Granted: #5053718, 5019789'. The datasheet cites new circuit techniques and special laser trimming of dynamic circuit performance for low harmonic distortion, plus a laser-trimmed offset. A copper leadframe improves heat dissipation. Supply is ±4.5 V to ±24 V (±25 V absolute maximum) per the datasheets, but a 2016 report says late OPA2604 production had to be held to ±20 V (see silicon_changes). It is unity-gain stable and drives 600 Ω. 'Difet' is a community label (Soomal 2016 groups OPA2604 with 'DiFET-structure' parts); the OPA2604 datasheet does not use the word.

reputation.summary: One of the defining 'Burr-Brown sound' op-amps. English forums call it warm, laid back and easy to listen to. Japanese PC-audio and headphone bloggers call it 'the legendary op-amp' (伝説のオペアンプ, e.g. southenst.com), with gloss (艶), spaciousness, fat bouncy bass and soft, smooth highs; nabe ranks it B+ (not re-verified). Soomal (2010) calls it an op-amp with a strong '胆味' (valve flavour), and Soomal (2013) says its fame among enthusiasts is 'not much lower than NE5532'. Soomal teardowns confirm it in the vivo Xplay and Xplay 3S (OPA2604AU), Smartisan T1, Sony PHA-3 (two as LPF after ES9018S), Shanling H3A (I/V and LPF), SoundAware M1 and A280III, TempoTec Serenade USB and Teclast T51. Its ±24 V rating made it one of the few audio op-amps usable on high rails. In a 2016 review Soomal rated warm DiFET-type parts (including OPA2604) above OPA1612-type parts for audio on average. Newer Japanese listening tests (new_western_elec 2025, not re-verified) rank it below MUSES8820/8920 and NL8802/NL8902.
sonic_descriptors: laid back, easy to listen to
typical_uses: CD player and DAC output / I-V stages (PCM DAC I/V converter is a datasheet application)
DAC low-pass filter stages (Sony PHA-3, Shanling H3A, SoundAware A280III/M1)
PC sound-card and USB DAC op-amp rolling
Headphone amplifiers
Smartphone Hi-Fi audio paths (vivo Xplay/Xplay 3S, Smartisan T1)
Maverick D2 DAC stock part; Fosi rolling kit (not re-verified)
Professional audio line stages on high (±18 to ±24 V) rails
caveats: Fast (20 MHz GBW): a translated English headphone-amp op-amp survey (translated by 杜毅 for DiyEden, reposted by Soomal 2005) reports that an OPA2604AP oscillated above about 18 V in one Hansen-type amp but ran at 34 VDC in other amps. The author called it much harder to use than OPA132/134 and heard it as nearly identical to them.

Needs adequate rails: the 0.0003% THD is specified at ±15 V. Soomal measured the Teclast T51 running it at about ±9.5 V and called the claim unachievable. Soomal said the Smartisan T1's OPA2604 showed high distortion, and that phones need a boost converter for it (T2 switched to OPA1612).
Soomal (2010, T51 context): driving low-impedance headphones directly makes it sound thin and harsh, with more bass distortion.
Some Japanese reviewers (Mineden) find the midrange thin (not re-verified).
Colored 'warm' voicing: 2025 Japanese tests prefer newer parts for resolution (not re-verified). Meizu's 2014 marketing showed a CMRR chart favouring OPA1612 over OPA2604.
OPA2604 (all packages) is EOL since c. 2016, so most market stock is fake (see counterfeit notes).

High-rail use is the weak point: TI E2E says OPA2604 performance could not be guaranteed near its ±24 V limit because of heat/package dissipation, and a 2016 diyAudio report says late parts had to be held to ±20 V (offset drift and rising Iq at ±24 V). Keep late-lot or unknown-origin OPA2604s at or below ±20 V.

silicon_changes.summary: Unannounced supply derating of the same part number: a document quoted on diyAudio (2016) says the OPA2604 no longer supports ±24 V and must be constrained to ±20 V, with long-term large offset drift and increased Iq at ±24 V (thought to be thermal). A TI E2E answer gives the same reason for the discontinuation (performance could not be guaranteed near the ±24 V limit because of heat/package dissipation). Whether a die or process change caused it is not known.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Only high-rail designs (±20 to ±24 V pro-audio line stages, some DIY amps) are at risk: offset drift and extra heat. Typical ±15 V op-amp rolling is unaffected.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - designs that rely on the OPA2604's unique ±24 V rating may drift or run hot with late lots; ±15 V use unaffected

families.counterfeit_notes: Fakes are extremely common for the OPA2604, and all remaining stock is post-EOL. A survey by the 'fakecomponents' account (19 Sep 2019) found 70 of 75 OPA2604s bought individually on Yahoo Auctions were fake (93%); the new_western_elec blog (Oct 2019) reported it and advised against buying there. The nabe blog has a 'fake-looking TI op-amp' post, and a Yahoo Chiebukuro Q&A discusses fake OPA2604s ordered from abroad. Reported fakes include remarked TL072-class dies, markings that wipe off with ethanol, and sanded or re-coated tops without moulded rounded edges on thinner bodies (not re-verified). Kokoro-navi (2011) reportedly documented fake OPA2134PA/OPA2604AP, and a fake was reported inside an Aune mini USB DAC (both not re-verified). TI E2E has an 'original or fake OPA2134/OPA2604' thread. Soomal (2010) compared a genuine part from a TI channel, a market fake and the chip pulled from a Teclast T51: the fake was obviously fake; the T51 chip differed from the genuine one only in marking clarity. Soomal stress-tested the T51 chip at ±23 V; it burned out, which proved nothing (and late genuine parts are reportedly not rated for ±24 V anyway). Tests: marking durability under solvent, package edge and mould finish, and parameters against the datasheet. A genuine OPA2604 draws about 10.5 mA total (max 12 mA at ±15 V) with 20 MHz GBW and 25 V/µs, versus about 3 MHz and 13 V/µs for a TL072 remark. Genuine SOIC parts are marked 'OPA 2604AU' (TI addendum). BB-logo and TI-logo lots are both genuine; no die change is documented, but late lots reportedly need rails held to ±20 V. Safest route: buy the still-active OPA604AP/AU from authorised distributors and use two on a dual adapter.
alternatives: OPA1656 (TI CMOS; named in a TI E2E FAQ as the 'next-generation OPA2134 and OPA2604 replacement'; ±2.25 V to ±18 V per SBOS901C, so not a ±24 V drop-in)
OPA1642 (TI JFET-input; suggested on TI E2E as a lower-noise, low-distortion OPA2604 alternative when 20 MHz is not needed; ±18 V max)
OPA2156 (TI CMOS; suggested on TI E2E when more bandwidth is needed; check supply limit before high-rail use)
OPA1688 (TI; reportedly suggested as an OPA2604 replacement, source not pinned down; check its supply limit)
OPA604AP/AU singles on a dual DIP-8 adapter (single-channel sibling, ACTIVE on ti.com)
OPA2134 (sibling Burr-Brown FET audio op-amp, still in PDIP but lower bandwidth; ±18 V max)
MUSES8920 (Japanese community successor; 'keeps OPA2604 softness with wider stage')

families.name: OPA627 / OPA637 (Burr-Brown Difet precision JFET single; OPA637 decompensated, G>=5)
families.tagline: Burr-Brown's Difet JFET single, long called the 'king' of op-amp rolling and prized for detail and a smooth sound, with pA bias and 4.5 nV/rtHz noise.
families.technology: JFET-input single op-amp. The Burr-Brown datasheet describes a high-speed, dielectrically isolated complementary NPN/PNP process with laser-trimmed Difet input circuitry. The OPA627 is unity-gain stable. The OPA637 is decompensated and stable at gains of 5 or more. TI's current SBOS165C (Jan 2025) retitles the family 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers', and its revision history records that the Difet references were deleted.

lineage.notes: Difet successor to the OPA111. PSpice macromodels dated October 1990 prove the part existed by then. The oldest datasheet edition found reads 'Printed in U.S.A. March, 1998' (confirmed).

The datasheet became SBOS165 in 2000. Rev A reads 'SEPTEMBER 2000-REVISED OCTOBER 2015'. Rev B is dated April 2024. Rev C reads 'AUGUST 2000 - REVISED JANUARY 2025'. TI names the OPA828 as its suggested alternate. PSpice literature numbers are SBOM099/SBOC118 (OPA627) and SBOM101/SBOC119 (OPA637).
Reported to sell OPA627AM/DIP stock via DigiKey Marketplace. Not verified.

key_specs.condition: f = 10 kHz (front-page figure). The 1 kHz value was not captured.
OPA637 at G = 10 (confirmed). The OPA627 16 MHz is corroborated only by a third-party EDA library.

key_specs.value: 7.5 mA max per amplifier (about 7-7.5 mA observed)
key_specs.condition: Not confirmed via web. Taken from a third-party supply budget and community fake-check guides.
The OPA627 is unity-gain stable. The OPA637 is stable at G>=5.

reputation.summary: Widely treated as the benchmark audiophile JFET single that later JFET parts are compared against. It is called the 'king' on English-language forums and 'legendary' in Japanese reviews. Soomal (China) groups the OPA627/637 with Burr-Brown's DiFET parts as warm-leaning, with full mids, strong dynamics and a spacious sound, and says they resolve HF better than the OPA111/OPA2107. Soomal also rates the OPA637 slightly above the OPA627. Critics such as Leckerton note that in blind listening it does not clearly beat cheaper parts like the AD8610. None of these characterizations were re-verified in this pass.
sonic_descriptors: warm, easy to listen to (Soomal AE-9 swap, 2020)
typical_uses: DAC post-filter / I/V stages (HiFiMAN HM-901 uses an OPA627 with an OPA2107 in the LPF, per Soomal)
Headphone amp cards: HiFiMAN IEM, balanced and Minibox cards pair it with the BUF634, per Soomal
line buffers and preamps
phono and high-impedance inputs (pA bias)
op-amp rolling in sound cards and DACs via single-to-dual adapters
transimpedance / photodiode and instrumentation front ends
caveats: It is a single op-amp only, so dual sockets need an adapter board.
The OPA637 is unstable below a noise gain of about 5. Do not drop it into unity-gain buffer sockets.
Quiescent current is up to about 7.5 mA per amp, which means heat and battery drain.
It is one of the most counterfeited audiophile op-amps.
The DIP versions are obsolete, and in 2024 TI said the SOIC AU might not be packaged for a while (E2E 1386960).
The current TI datasheet shows pins 1/5 as NC on the molded packages, and offset trim applies to the TO-99 only.
Soomal folklore that country of origin matters (US > Taiwan > SE Asia) is not backed by any measurements.
A/B-grade differences are reportedly inaudible, and blind tests reportedly show no clear win over the AD8610. Neither claim was re-verified.

In the current pin table, molded-package pins 1/5 are NC, and the datasheet says the external offset pot applies to TO-99 only. No date-code cut-over or PCN was found.
silicon_changes.summary: TI's 2024-2025 rewrite deleted the 'Difet' wording, added a new B-grade SOIC (OPA627BU), and dropped offset-trim pins on the molded packages. For the sister OPA132, which also has trim pins changed to NC, TI E2E 1517005 attributes the change to higher-precision manufacturing that makes trim unnecessary. diyAudio users cite 'newer, more efficient manufacturing processes'. In 2024, TI E2E 1386960 said the AU was temporarily not being packaged while BU and TO-can stock was coming. That points to a new die or trim process under the same part numbers, but TI has not confirmed a silicon change for the OPA627 and no PCN was found.

families.counterfeit_notes: One of the most counterfeited audiophile op-amps. In 2014, ZeptoBars decapped a $2.7 'OPA627' from China/eBay and found an Analog Devices AD744 die (marked 'AD'/'B744'). The genuine die shows at least 4 laser-trimmed resistors and the fake shows 1; the AD744 has about 3x the noise and 0.5 mV offset against 0.1 mV. OPA602 and AD711-class donor dies are also reported but were not verified. Community checks (Head-Fi, diyAudio, not re-verified) are quiescent current of about 7-7.5 mA plus square-wave and slew tests. The pin 1-5 trim-resistance check is unreliable on new TI molded parts, whose pins 1/5 are NC. Maimai-audio (a single blog) lists OPA627AU lot codes A3L, AEB, AKG, D5L, K4D, LAE, LDE, LPS, MDE and T3K as almost all fake. Soomal makes several points: TO-99 OPA637BM selling for tens of yuan are fake; every 'custom metal-can' version is fake; some fakes put an ordinary PDIP chip inside a metal shell; and SM parts are very rare. The DIP versions are obsolete, so any 'new' OPA627AP/BP is suspect. Buy the SOIC AU/BU from TI or an authorized distributor.
alternatives: OPA828 / OPA2828 (TI's suggested alternate for the OPA627. TI E2E 1386960 names the OPA828ID as a pin-to-pin replacement for the OPA627AU. TI describes it as 'the next generation OPA627 and OPA827'.)
OPA827 (TI low-noise JFET single)
ADA4627-1 / ADA4637-1 (ADI JFET; the ADA4637 is the decompensated analogue of the OPA637)
AD8610 / AD8620 (ADI JFET)
MUSES01 (Nisshinbo/JRC JFET dual)

claims_confirmed: SBOS165C is current, with the header 'AUGUST 2000 - REVISED JANUARY 2025'. The Rev C history records the OPA627BU changing from preview to production and gives the Rev B date as April 2024 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
The current title is 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers' (https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/OPA627 ; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa637.pdf).
The revision history records that the Difet references were deleted and the OPA627BU preview device was added (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
SBOS165A reads 'SEPTEMBER 2000-REVISED OCTOBER 2015' and includes ESD ratings of HBM +/-2500 V and CDM +/-1000 V for SOIC (https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/opa627-406898.pdf).

The Rev A copy shows 'Trim 5 Trim 1' and 'Product Folder / Sample & Buy' (https://www.cimarrontechnology.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/opa627.pdf ; https://datasheets.b-cdn.net/files/OPA627AU-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-60566259.pdf).

Molded-package trim pins are now NC and offset adjustment applies to TO-99 only (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/opa132-opa627-and-other-ti-bb-op-amps-no-longer-have-an-offset-trim-terminal.418419/).

TI attributes the NC trim pins on the OPA132 (from Rev C) to higher-precision manufacturing (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1517005/opa132-changed-opa132-pin-1-and-pin-8-from-offset-trim-to-nc).

In 2024, TI said the OPA627AU was still active but 'will not be packaged for now', named the OPA828ID as a pin-to-pin replacement, and said BU/TO-can stock would come shortly (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/1386960/opa627-is-the-opa627au-end-of-life).

OPA627AP is obsolete (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/OPA627AP/251165 ; https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/1370897/opa627-opa627ap-product-problem).
OPA637: 80 MHz GBW at G=10, 135 V/us slew, product ACTIVE (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637).
The OPA627BU and OPA637AU orderable pages exist (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA627/part-details/OPA627BU ; https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637/part-details/OPA637AU).
OPA627: 4.5 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, 55 V/us, 100 uV max Vos, 0.8 uV/C, 5 pA max IB, +/-4.5 to +/-18 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).

The Burr-Brown edition is 'Printed in U.S.A. March, 1998' and describes a dielectrically isolated complementary NPN/PNP process with laser-trimmed Difet input (https://instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/OPA627.pdf ; https://www.audiophonics.fr/images2/8434/opa627.pdf).

families.technology: JFET (FET) input voltage-feedback op-amp. Burr-Brown design, datasheet origin January 1995 (Burr-Brown macromodel dated Feb 1996). lineage.notes: Datasheet origin 'JANUARY 1995'. The Burr-Brown OPA132 macromodel dates from 02/23/96 (REV. A 7/20/96). The OPA134 macromodel says 'adapted from OPA132 model 9/24/96', and CMoy pages call the OPA134 'the audio-specific version of the OPA132'. The OPA132 was the op-amp in Chu Moy's original pocket amp.

SBOS054 revisions: A (revised June 2004), B (revised September 2015) and C (revised August 2024). Rev C changed OPA132 pins 1/8 from Offset Trim to NC. Per TI E2E, this followed a new-fab/design change with an improved process, affecting all package types. The PDIP singles (OPA132P/PA) and the PDIP quad (OPA4132PA) are obsolete; the SOIC parts are active. The TI PSpice model OPA132.LIB (Final 1.2, 05FEB2019) references SBOS054B.
